senses.gloss:
अमृत अ-मृत.
 I. adj., f. ता, Immortal, Bhag. 14, 27.
 II. m.
 1. A god.
 2. The soul.
 III. n.
 1. The beverage of the gods, nectar.
 2. A medicine preventing old age, prolonging life, and awakening the dead, Lass. 33, 20.
 3. A medicament; nectar and medicament, Śiś. 9, 36.
 4. The residue of sacrificial food, Man. 3, 285.
 5. Unsolicited alms, Man. 4, 4.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. ἄμβροτος, ἀμβροσία.
अमृतत्व अमृत + त्व, n. Immortality, Man. 6, 60.
अमृतमय अमृत + मय, adj., f. यी, Like nectar, Pañc. 206, 7.
अमृतलतिका अमृतलतिका, i. e. अमृत-लता + क, f. A small creeper as beautiful as nectar (denoting a beautiful woman), Śrut. (Br.) 35.
अमृत- + लतिका अमृत- + लतिका, f. a creeper yielding nectar. Śrut. 35 (Brockhaus).
अमृतस्रुत् अमृत-स्रु + त्, adj. Shedding nectar, Śiś. 5, 68.
अमृताय अमृताय denom. derived from अमृत by य, Ātm. To be like nectar, Ragh. 2, 61.
अमृत- + उपम अमृत- + उपम, adj., f. मा, Amṛta-like, Nal. 12, 58.
अमृत- + कुण्ड अमृत- + कुण्ड, n. the vessel containing the अमृत, or beverage of immortality.
अमृत- + द्रव अमृत- + द्रव, adj., f. वा, flowing with Amṛta (and medicaments), Śiś. 9, 36.
अमृत- + मन्थन अमृत- + मन्थन, n. production [] of the Amṛta, the beverage of the gods, by churning, MBh. vol. i. p. 41, l. 2.
अ- + मृषा अ- + मृषा, adv. truly.

अमृत- + रस अमृत- + रस,
 I. m. the amṛta essence, the drink of immortality, Bhartṛ. 3, 77 (काव्य-, poetical works which are like the essence of amṛta).
 II. adj., f. सा, having an amṛta-like juice, Pañc. 248, 12.
अमृत- + लता अमृत- + लता, f. a creeper yielding nectar, Bhartṛ. 1, 75.

अमृत- + सेक अमृत- + सेक, m. sprinkling with the beverage of the gods, Hit. ii. d. 132 (फलन्त्य् अमृतसेके ऽपि पथ्यानि विषद्रुमाः, ‘Poisonous trees, although sprinkled with nectar, do not bear healthy fruits’).
अ-मृत- + आस्वादनीय अ-मृत- + आस्वाद्नीय, adj. as pleasant to the taste as nectar, MBh. 3, 1740.
